elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience (Agreement and/or Order Form)
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term."
"upon 30 days' prior written notice" (shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee appears in the inserted Section 9.4.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Vendor has no right to terminate ... for convenience during a committed term" — no end-of-term 90-day Vendor right granted
Single inserted Section 9.4 via insert_after p0038; no other paragraph altered

reasons: The inserted Section 9.4 delivers all four preferred atomic elements: Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata), and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term.

Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (30 days is below the 60–90 day band, no early-termination fee, no end-of-term Vendor right), but that is irrelevant because the locked target is preferred and the preferred bargain is complete.

Minimal: one concise insertion filling a genuinely absent clause, with no rewrite of Sections 2.1, 8.1, 9.1–9.3 or 9.5 and no imported fallback mechanics (the fee/60-day alternative is offered only in the non-operative comment).

Intent preserved: numbering 9.4 slots correctly between 9.3 and 9.5, all defined terms used (Fees, Order Form, Vendor) are resolved, and no dangling mechanic is created. The residual tension with Section 2.1's "without reduction or termination rights" pre-exists (Sections 9.1–9.3 already grant termination rights and 8.1 contemplates earlier termination); worth noting in the rationale that a conforming carve-out in 2.1 would remove any argument that the take-or-pay commitment survives a convenience termination.
